display.title: Tanya Shiur 20: Chapters 15 and 16, Serving Hashem Beyond Habit
display.summary_short: Two Yiddish Tanya shiurim on chapters 15 and 16: who is called 'one who serves G-d', why going beyond habit matters, and how Hashem joins a good thought to the deed.
display.summary_long: This recording holds two consecutive shiurim from Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series. The first continues chapter 15: a beinoni who keeps every mitzvah but does so by nature or habit is called 'one who does not serve', while one who pushes past his nature is 'one who serves G-d'. He explains the Gemara's teaching that reviewing a lesson 101 times rather than 100 makes the difference, with the parable of donkey drivers who charged double for the eleventh mile, and parables of a sundial's shadow and the Baal Shem Tov's way of drawing out 'Baruch Hashem'. Stories include a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe lost in meditation for hours, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's Shabbos lamp that burned on vinegar. The second shiur reviews chapter 15 with the parable of a wick that must be consumed to give light, talks about guarding one's speech and the prayer 'Elokai netzor' at the end of Shemoneh Esrei, then studies chapter 16: ruling over one's nature through contemplating Hashem's greatness, and the comfort that Hashem joins even a hidden love and fear in the mind to the deed, so the mitzvah rises above. Stories of the Baal Shem Tov weeping in a beis midrash and of the Alter Rebbe's longing for Hashem are woven in.
display.lesson: Real service of Hashem means stepping a little beyond one's nature and habits; and even when feelings stay hidden in the mind, Hashem joins a good intention to the deed and lifts the mitzvah up.

study_text.note: Two shiurim in one file: the first continues chapter 15; the second reviews chapter 15 and studies chapter 16 to its end.

characters: a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe lost in meditation
a professor who examined the Alter Rebbe

segments.title: Shiur A: Tanya chapter 15, one who serves and one who does not
segments.summary: A beinoni whose good conduct comes by nature or habit, versus one who goes beyond his nature.

segments.title: Diligence that became second nature
segments.summary: Even diligence acquired by effort, once it is habit, no longer counts as 'service'.

segments.title: 101 times: the donkey drivers' parable
segments.summary: The Gemara's teaching on reviewing a lesson a hundred and one times, explained with the price of an eleventh mile.

segments.title: A small bend: the sundial's shadow
segments.summary: A tiny movement of the shadow reflects a vast journey of the sun, like a small act of self-mastery above.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov and 'Baruch Hashem'
segments.summary: The Baal Shem Tov would ask Jews how they were so they would answer with praise of Hashem.

segments.title: A Chassid lost in meditation
segments.summary: A Chassid of the Alter Rebbe stood for hours with one foot on a wagon axle, not noticing the wagon had left.

segments.title: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's vinegar lamp
segments.summary: The One who told oil to burn can tell vinegar to burn, and the Shabbos lamp stayed lit.

segments.title: Shiur B: review of chapter 15 and Tanya chapter 16
segments.summary: Review of the beinoni levels, then chapter 16 on ruling over one's nature and on Hashem joining a good thought to the deed.

segments.title: Review: the wick and the oil
segments.summary: A wick gives light only by being consumed, and so a person must give something of himself.

segments.title: Guarding one's speech and 'Elokai netzor'
segments.summary: Holding back a sharp word, and why the prayer to guard the tongue comes at the end of Shemoneh Esrei.

segments.title: Chapter 16: the great rule, contemplating Hashem's greatness
segments.summary: The beinoni rules over his nature by contemplating Hashem's greatness, illustrated by the parable of the mountains and the sky.

segments.title: When love and fear stay hidden in the mind
segments.summary: A beinoni whose understanding does not reach his heart, and the wings that lift a mitzvah.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov weeps in a beis midrash
segments.summary: Torah learned without love and fear of Hashem stays below, and the Baal Shem Tov wept over it.

segments.title: The Alter Rebbe's longing for Hashem
segments.summary: A professor who examined the Alter Rebbe sensed a longing he could not grasp.

segments.title: Hashem joins a good thought to the deed
segments.summary: Hashem bridges the gap between hidden understanding and action, so the mitzvah rises to the higher worlds.
